blocks.title: Complex Plane and Absolute Value
teacherCues: Draw a complex plane, label real axis (horizontal) and imaginary axis (vertical). Plot point (a,b) for a+bi.
Ask: How do you find the distance from the origin? (√(a²+b²))

discoveryHook.scenario: Just like a GPS coordinate, a complex number has a location on a flat map. Its distance from the origin is the 'modulus'—essentially how far it is from zero.

explanation: The [[kw:complex plane]] has a horizontal real axis and a vertical imaginary axis. Each complex number z = a+bi is plotted at (a,b).
The [[kw:absolute value]] (or modulus) of z, denoted |z|, is the distance from the origin: $$|z| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}.$$
If b=0 (real number), this reduces to the usual absolute value.

examples.title: A – Plot and find |z|
examples.prompt: Plot z = -2+5i and find its absolute value.

examples.title: B – Real number case
examples.prompt: Explain why | -7 | as a real number equals |-7+0i|.
examples.peerPrompt: In the complex plane, what are the coordinates? Then apply the modulus formula.

confusionCorner.title: Imaginary part includes the sign
confusionCorner.body: The coordinate for the imaginary axis is b, the coefficient of i, so include its sign. For -7i, b=-7.

questions.prompt: In the complex plane, the horizontal axis is the ___ axis.
hints: It corresponds to the real part of a+bi.
Use the formula √(a²+b²) with a=3, b=4.

questions.prompt: What is the imaginary part (b) of 2-5i? (Enter a number)
hints: The imaginary part is the coefficient of i.

blocks.title: Adding Complex Numbers Geometrically
teacherCues: Draw vectors u=⟨1,3⟩ and v=⟨2,1⟩. The sum u+v=⟨3,4⟩ corresponds to (1+3i)+(2+i)=3+4i.
Emphasize: add the real parts, add the imaginary parts; geometrically, use the parallelogram law.

discoveryHook.scenario: Adding complex numbers is like combining two moves on a city grid: one step right/up for the first number, then another step for the second.

explanation: To add complex numbers geometrically, represent each as a vector from the origin. The sum is the vector obtained by the [[kw:parallelogram law]] (or tip‑to‑tail).
The graphical sum corresponds exactly to component addition.

formulaCard.title: Addition
notes: Add real parts, add imaginary parts.

examples.title: A – Sum of two numbers
steps: Result: 3+4i. The vectors ⟨1,3⟩ and ⟨2,1⟩ sum to ⟨3,4⟩.

examples.title: B – Geometric interpretation
examples.prompt: Explain how (3+i)+(1+2i) = 4+3i corresponds to vector addition.
examples.peerPrompt: Describe the vectors, draw them, and show the sum vector.

confusionCorner.title: Imaginary unit i is not a variable
confusionCorner.body: i is not a variable; just combine its coefficients. Don't forget the sign.

questions.prompt: To add complex numbers geometrically, you use the ___ law of vector addition.
hints: It's the method where you place vectors tail to tail and draw the diagonal.

questions.prompt: Add (5+2i) + (3+4i). Write the result as a+bi (e.g., 8+6i).
hints: Add the real parts, then add the imaginary parts.

questions.prompt: Geometrically, the sum of two complex numbers is represented by the ___ from the origin to the opposite corner of the parallelogram.
hints: Think of the parallelogram formed by the two vectors.
The result is the line connecting opposite corners.

blocks.title: Subtracting and Complex Conjugates
teacherCues: Subtraction: (4+2i) - (3-i) = (4-3)+(2-(-1))i = 1+3i. Geometrically, add the opposite vector.
Plot z = -3+i and its conjugate -3-i. Note reflection across real axis.

discoveryHook.scenario: Subtracting a complex number is like adding its mirror image in reverse; the conjugate is a simple reflection across the horizontal axis.

explanation: Subtraction: (a+bi) - (c+di) = (a-c)+(b-d)i. Geometrically, this is u - v = u + (-v).
The [[kw:complex conjugate]] of a+bi is a-bi. In the complex plane, it is a reflection across the real axis.

formulaCard.title: Subtraction & Conjugate
notes: Subtract real parts, subtract imaginary parts.
Conjugate changes the sign of the imaginary part only.

examples.title: A – Subtract vectors
steps: Write as u - v with u=⟨4,2⟩, v=⟨3,-1⟩.
Geometrically, add u and -v=⟨-3,1⟩ to get ⟨1,3⟩.

examples.title: B – Conjugate
examples.prompt: Plot z=2-3i and its conjugate. Write the conjugate.
examples.peerPrompt: Where is the reflection? Which sign changes?
steps: Conjugate is 2+3i. The point (2,-3) reflects across the real axis to (2,3).

confusionCorner.title: Double negative
confusionCorner.body: When subtracting a negative imaginary part, watch the sign: (a+bi) - (c+di) when d is negative becomes plus.

questions.prompt: The complex conjugate of a+bi is a-bi. The points are reflections across the ___ axis.
hints: The reflection flips the sign of the imaginary part.
Change the sign of the imaginary part only.
The real part stays the same.

questions.prompt: To subtract complex numbers geometrically, you add the ___ of the second vector.
hints: You reverse the direction of the subtracted vector.

blocks.title: Distance in the Complex Plane
teacherCues: Write the Distance Formula: d = √((s-a)² + (t-b)²). It's just the modulus of the difference.

discoveryHook.scenario: How far apart are two ships on a radar screen? Treat their positions as complex numbers and compute the distance.

explanation: The distance between two complex numbers a+bi and s+ti is the modulus of their difference: $$d = \sqrt{(s-a)^2 + (t-b)^2}.$$
This is the same as the Euclidean distance between points (a,b) and (s,t).

examples.title: B – Modulus of difference
examples.prompt: Show that the distance is the modulus of (5-2i) - (2+3i).
examples.peerPrompt: Compute the difference, then its modulus. Compare with the previous result.

confusionCorner.title: Order doesn't matter for distance
confusionCorner.body: Whether you compute z₁-z₂ or z₂-z₁, the modulus is the same.

questions.prompt: The distance between two complex numbers is the modulus of their ___.
hints: What operation do you perform to find the vector between them?

questions.prompt: What is the distance between 0 and 5i? (Enter a number)
For points (a,b) and (s,t), the distance formula is √((s-a)² + (t-___)²).
hints: It's the difference of the imaginary parts.

blocks.title: Blueprint Aid – Midpoint in the Complex Plane
teacherCues: Write the Midpoint Formula: ((a+s)/2, (b+t)/2). This gives the average of the coordinates.

discoveryHook.scenario: Finding the halfway point between two cities on a map uses the same idea as finding the midpoint of two complex numbers.

explanation: [[imp:Understand]]: We need the midpoint of the segment joining points corresponding to z₁ = a+bi and z₂ = s+ti.
[[imp:Conclude]]: This point corresponds to the complex number $$\frac{a+s}{2} + \frac{b+t}{2}i.$$

formulaCard.title: Midpoint Formula
notes: Averages the real and imaginary parts separately.
The result is a complex number.

examples.title: A – Find midpoint
examples.prompt: Find the midpoint of the segment joining 4-3i and 2+2i.

examples.title: B – Verify with distance
examples.prompt: Show that the midpoint is equidistant from both endpoints.
examples.peerPrompt: Compute distance from midpoint to each endpoint using the distance formula.

confusionCorner.title: Keep the imaginary part sign
confusionCorner.body: When averaging imaginary parts, include the sign. For -3 and +2, sum is -1, divided by 2 is -0.5.

questions.prompt: The midpoint of the segment joining (a,b) and (s,t) is ((a+s)/2, ___/2).
hints: Add b and t, then divide by 2.

questions.prompt: Find the midpoint of 1+4i and 7+2i. Write as a+bi (e.g., 4+3i).
In the complex plane, the midpoint formula gives a point that is ___ from both endpoints.
hints: The midpoint is the same distance to each end.

challengeCorner.prompt: If the midpoint of two complex numbers is 2+i and one endpoint is 5+3i, find the other endpoint.
